correctness.rationale: The 21-dimensional quintic first-jet interpolation map is injective by degree-five restriction with three double zeros on every one of seven rational lines, and hence bijective. Exactly 3^7=2187 tangent assignments arise uniquely. The 168-element PGL3(F2) action partitions assignments into 18 explicitly listed orbits. Reconstructed exact binary Gröbner unit-ideal checks on all three affine charts certify geometric singularity/non-singularity for each representative. Two independent exact algebra implementations agree. The result yields 420+924+168=1512 smooth assignments in 10 orbits and 567+24+84=675 singular ones; concurrency is checked via rank of the three tangent line covectors. A separate all-quintic enumeration corroborates the smooth total.

originality.rationale: The contribution is a necessary-and-sufficient Fano-point tangent incidence criterion for geometric smoothness of 2187 locally smooth plane-filling quintics, with an exceptional concurrency obstruction and three exact good Gauss-fiber profiles. Asgarli–Ghioca analyze plane-filling smooth curves but not all tangent assignments; the complete Huang–Kedlaya–Lau genus-six census covers all smooth equations and thereby subsumes the aggregate 1512 count and 10-orbit census, but the inspected section and associated README do not state the global-smoothness iff test in local jet data. Source, alias, parameter and implication searches disclosed below did not identify this theorem. Search incompleteness and possible derivability from the 2024 complete data remain publication-priority risks.

value.rationale: For the natural minimal plane-filling degree-five genus-six problem in characteristic two, the seven rational first jets are a complete local input, yet geometric smoothness over an algebraic closure is global. The newly explicit iff test using only tangent-fiber multiplicities and whether three doubled rational tangent lines concur makes that local-to-global phenomenon structural, rules out a nonobvious 84-configuration obstruction, and distinguishes different rational Gauss-map ramification profiles. It is not just a fixed parameter count copied from the published full-curve census.
